correctness.rationale: For an eight-point representation, the forbidden mono/dichromatic triangles make each colour a 1-factor, hence the colouring is a one-factorization of K8. A pair of factors forming two 4-cycles exposes only four closing diagonals and therefore cannot realize all five possible third colours, so qualitative coverage implies perfectness. Conversely, if a triple is missing in a perfect one-factorization, the third factor avoids cycle edges and all eight distance-two chords of an alternating Hamiltonian 8-cycle; the seven possible remaining perfect matchings are exhausted and every one makes a 4+4 union with one alternating factor, contradicting perfectness. Published enumeration gives one perfect class. The published unique-extension theorem then reduces seven-point classes to vertex orbits, which the verifier computes as 1+7.

value.rationale: K8 is the first complete-graph order at which one-factorizations branch into multiple isomorphism classes after the unique K4 and K6 cases. The qualitative condition selects one of six classes and its nontransitive 1+7 vertex action produces two distinct seven-point representations, turning a general existence theorem into a complete first-branching moduli calculation.
